hints: Use the Pythagorean identity $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$ to simplify the equation to $1 + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 1 \implies 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 0$.
walkthrough:
Expand the square on the left-hand side of $(\cos\theta + \sin\theta)^2 = 1$:
$$\cos^2\theta + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$$

Set each trigonometric factor to zero:
$$\sin\theta = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad \cos\theta = 0$$

Solve for $\theta$ in the interval $0 \le \theta \le \pi$:
$$\sin\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 0, \pi$$
$$\cos\theta = 0 \implies \theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$$
Thus, the three solutions are $\theta = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi$.

hints: Since squaring introduces possible extraneous roots, test all three candidate solutions from part (a)(i) in the unsquared equation $\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1$.
walkthrough:
Test each of the three candidate roots $\theta = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi$ from (a)(i) in the original linear equation $\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1$:
$$\text{For } \theta = 0: \quad \cos 0 + \sin 0 = 1 + 0 = 1 \quad (\text{valid})$$
$$\text{For } \theta = \frac{\pi}{2}: \quad \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0 + 1 = 1 \quad (\text{valid})$$
$$\text{For } \theta = \pi: \quad \cos\pi + \sin\pi = -1 + 0 = -1 \neq 1 \quad (\text{invalid})$$
Conclude that the only solutions on $0 \le \theta \le \pi$ are $\theta = 0$ and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$.

hints: Put the left-hand side over a common denominator $(\cos\theta + \sin\theta)(\cos\theta - \sin\theta) = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$.
Use $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$ in the denominator to reach $1 - 2\sin^2\theta$.
walkthrough:
Combine the two fractions on the left-hand side over a common denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin\theta(\cos\theta - \sin\theta) + (1 - \cos\theta)(\cos\theta + \sin\theta)}{(\cos\theta + \sin\theta)(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)}$$

Combine the simplified numerator and denominator to complete the identity:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\cos\theta + \sin\theta - 1}{1 - 2\sin^2\theta} = \text{RHS}$$

hints: Substitute the identity from part (b) into the equation: $\frac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1}{1-2\sin^2\theta} = 2(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)$.
walkthrough:
Replace the left-hand side using the proved identity from part (b):
$$\frac{\cos\theta + \sin\theta - 1}{1 - 2\sin^2\theta} = 2(\cos\theta + \sin\theta - 1)$$

Case 1: $\cos\theta + \sin\theta - 1 = 0$
$$\text{From part (a)(ii), the solutions in } [0, \pi] \text{ are } \theta = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}$$

Combine all solutions on the interval $0 \le \theta \le \pi$:
$$\theta = 0, \; \frac{\pi}{6}, \; \frac{\pi}{2}, \; \frac{5\pi}{6}$$
